title: atpE and bedaquiline binding
dek: AtpE is the c-ring of ATP synthase, the binding site. High-level BDQ resistance, rare in surveys. Most clinical BDQ MIC shifts are Rv0678, not atpE. Reporting “no atpE mutation ⇒ BDQ-S” is incomplete.
story: Bedaquiline binds the c-subunit of mycobacterial F-ATP synthase, encoded by atpE, and uncouples/blocks ATP synthesis. Target-site substitutions (D28N, A63P, I66M and kin) produce high-level BDQ resistance. They are uncommon in programmatic surveys compared with Rv0678 loss-of-function.
Because they are rare, a naive lab that only looks at atpE will systematically call BDQ-S in isolates that pump the drug out. Put atpE and Rv0678 (and pepQ) on the same line of the SOP.
ATP synthase is essential, which is probably why atpE missense is rare and often costly. That does not make the alleles unimportant when present — they veto BDQ hard.
deepTitle: What to put in the report
deep: An atpE graded R allele is a stop-BPaLM event even if Rv0678 is clean.
WT atpE is the beginning of a BDQ sentence, not the end.
Do not confuse atpE with atpC or with the host mitochondrial synthase. Mtb numbering, Mtb gene.
MIC remains useful: target-site mutants sit far to the right; efflux mutants sit modestly right-shifted and can overlap CC.

visual.caption: BDQ has a binding-site gene (atpE) and a common clinical resistance gene (Rv0678 → MmpL5). Both must be read.

example.title: atpE WT, Rv0678 frameshift
example.setup: Report draft: “No atpE mutation, BDQ susceptible.” Rv0678 has a frameshift AF 0.99.

steps.title: Rewrite the sentence
steps.body: atpE WT only excludes the rare high-level target path.

steps.title: Grade the frameshift
steps.body: LOF in Rv0678 is the common BDQ/CFZ MIC-up route. Catalogue + MIC if you can.

steps.title: Regimen
steps.body: Do not count BDQ as a solid Group A drug without humility. This may be a leave-BPaLM moment depending on grade and MIC.

example.takeaway: atpE is necessary to look at and insufficient to clear BDQ.
